transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad to meet you today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I keep getting these really distressing, unwanted memories of a traumatic event that happened to me. It feels like I'm constantly reliving it through sudden, vivid flashbacks, and I just can't seem to make them stop. It has gotten to the point where I really need some help dealing with them.
I'm so sorry you're going through this. When did this traumatic event occur, and how long have you been experiencing these flashbacks and memories?
The traumatic event happened about a year ago. I have been experiencing these constant flashbacks and intrusive memories ever since, so it has been going on for the past 12 months.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Posttraumatic Stress Disorder, Acute Stress Disorder, and Adjustment Disorder. Since the traumatic event occurred a year ago and the symptoms (intrusive memories and flashbacks) have persisted for 12 months, Acute Stress Disorder is ruled out because its duration is limited to 3 days to 1 month. Adjustment Disorder is also ruled out because the patient's symptoms meet the full criteria for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder, which is the more specific diagnosis.

inference_history.note: The patient presents with intrusive, distressing memories and vivid flashbacks of a traumatic event, which strongly points toward trauma- and stressor-related disorders. At this early stage of the interview, Posttraumatic Stress Disorder, Acute Stress Disorder, and Adjustment Disorder are the primary differential diagnoses. Further history regarding the timeline, duration, and other associated symptoms is needed to differentiate them.
